Adampol – Polonezköy

Founders' memorial, 150th anniversary (Czartoryski and Czajkowski)

'A Polish village on Turkish soil' – so says the stone that 'grateful Adampol residents and compatriots from Poland' raised to the village's founders on its 150th anniversary.

Theme
Adampol – Polonezköy
District
Beykoz
Period
1842 / 1992
Visiting
Limited access

The story

A prince who ran the settlement from Paris and a writer who changed his name and his faith – these are the two faces looking out from this stone. The plaque with their medallions was set up in 1992 for the village's 150th anniversary.

The text, in Polish and Turkish, says that Adampol, 'a Polish village on Turkish soil', was founded in 1842 by Prince Adam Czartoryski (1770–1861), an outstanding Polish statesman, and by Michał Czajkowski – Mehmed Sadyk Pasha (1804–1886), writer, political activist and later commander of the Sultan's Cossacks. It was put up by 'grateful Adampol residents and compatriots from Poland'.

How to visit

The stone stands in the churchyard of the Church of Our Lady of Częstochowa at the western end of the village (the pin is approximate). Stand facing it: the upper text is in Polish, the lower in Turkish, with the two medallions and the founders' life dates in between. Nearby there is a second 1842–1992 plaque with the Polish eagle and the Turkish crescent. The churchyard may be closed outside opening hours – check them before you go.
